### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s).

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `resolveService (12 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d658ad2857e72f4fa3747debc1d4ea1cfae3ee0` — the merge of head `b14cd22b091c973347e070876eb7da5c6b7fac4b` into base `8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d658ad2857e72f4fa3747debc1d4ea1cfae3ee0 && git checkout 7d658ad2857e72f4fa3747debc1d4ea1cfae3ee0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91 b14cd22b091c973347e070876eb7da5c6b7fac4b && git checkout -B drift-repro 8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91 && git merge --no-ff b14cd22b091c973347e070876eb7da5c6b7fac4b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5eb211c44992f6bbb689cb4e0f068fb6ed783f88`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/multi-replica-package-refusal.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.ts (the narrowing face: every non-prose path of the diff; the three test files were read as evidence, the changeset is a prose face for the lane seat's ACCEPT)

Faces: schema (`hits` = the ledger) AND a declared narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). Inputs: card #31599 body and comments 6724381346 (triage), 6727421428 (claim), 6728532665 (amendment), 6730804450 (os-dev-report, read as the dev's claim); PR #31751 body, file list (9 files) and the net diff against `main` at `cae8d8fe` (merge-base of the head); the check-runs on the head; the prior record on PR #31712 (comment 6728523407) as the reference for how the ledger row was judged. The cloud repository is not readable from this session: D1 and R3 are judged as the card body quotes them verbatim. Code outside the diff (`@objectstack/service-cluster` `multi-replica.ts`, the dispatcher, the metadata protocol's ensure door, `@objectstack/metadata-core`'s pair lookup) was read to judge the diff, never reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Narrowing of the seven package doors — RIGHT.** On a deployment where `declaresMultiNode(process.env)` holds (`OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS` greater than 1, or `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true`) and the composed `cluster` service's `driver` is `redis`, `POST /packages`, `PATCH /:id/enable`, `PATCH /:id/disable`, `POST /:id/duplicate`, `POST /:id/ensure-customization`, `PATCH /:id` and `DELETE /:id` answer `409 MULTI_REPLICA_PACKAGE_CHANGE_REFUSED`. Read in the tree: at each of the seven sites `refuseMultiReplicaPackageChange` sits after `requireManageMetadata` and `refuseWalledCatalogPackageWrite` and before `refusePackageWriteDoorQuery`, the body parse, the protocol resolve and every registry read, so nothing is read or written first. This is D1 「多副本时拒绝」 on exactly the doors the card names (create/ensure, enable, disable, install/uninstall, plus duplicate and manifest edit as siblings that change the registry), and R3's two conjuncts: the condition is `declaresMultiReplicaOnRedis` imported from `@objectstack/service-cluster` (card item 2, "whichever lands second imports the first"), never a local spelling. A single node, `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS=1`, the in-process driver (escape hatch included), any other driver and no composed cluster service all answer `false` and the doors run as on `main`.
2. **Sibling doors left unrefused — RIGHT, with the bound stated.** The other seven walled sites in `packages.ts` (publish, publish-drafts, discard-drafts, commit revert, rollback, revert, adopt-orphans) are not refused. publish-drafts, discard-drafts, commit revert, rollback and adopt-orphans write `sys_metadata` rows through the protocol, which every replica reads: outside D1's set (registry or package state). `POST /:id/publish` and `POST /:id/revert` reach `MetadataManager.publishPackage` / `revertPackage`, the metadata service's own item registry, not the package registry or the package-state store: also outside D1's named set, and the metadata domain's replication is the metadata cluster bridge's concern (another #3814 card), not this one's. Recorded as the bound, not a finding.
3. **Clone doors — RIGHT in the rule, WRONG in the derivation (must-fix, ④.2).** The rule the PR declares, ledger row included, is: refuse only when the default landing would CREATE the source's paired customization package on this replica; reuse of a pair this replica already serves, and an explicit writable target, create no package and land as before. The rule is correct under D1 (a reuse writes nothing per-replica; the copy itself is a shared metadata row). The tree does not implement the rule for every base: see ④.2.
4. **Published-face widening — RIGHT in the tree and in the declaration.** `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER['@objectstack/runtime']` gains `MULTI_REPLICA_PACKAGE_CHANGE_REFUSED`. The `ErrorCode` union is unchanged (the code is already a member through the cloud-connection row), so no reference page regenerates (`check:docs` inside the green lint jobs; the file list holds no `content/docs` change). The widening is the per-package tuple of the exported ledger, a published face, and the ledger's own rule asks for it: 「a code emitted by several packages is listed once per emitting package」. The seat's amendment 6728532665 names exactly this as the `yes` half. The prior record's ③ Q1(i) foresaw the row as the dev's duty, not the gate's (the runtime stamps are identifier stamps, `{ code: MULTI_REPLICA_PACKAGE_CHANGE_REFUSED }` and `Object.assign(new Error(...), { statusCode: 409, code: ... })`, in the provenance gate's declared blind spot): done.
5. **Provenance — RIGHT.** The waiver `(service-cluster, MULTI_REPLICA_PACKAGE_CHANGE_REFUSED, registeredUnder cloud-connection)` still holds in the gate's three directions on this head: the cloud-connection key lists the code, the ledger has no `@objectstack/service-cluster` owner key, the `constdef` site in `multi-replica.ts` is untouched. A second owner-key row is not a second waiver and makes none dead weight. `Lint · docs & code guards` (which runs `check:error-code-provenance`): success on the head.
6. **Envelope — RIGHT.** The package doors answer through `deps.error(message, 409, { code })`, the same construction the walled refusal and the capability gate use, so `details.code` is promoted into `error.code` by the shared builder; the permission-set door throws an ADR-0112 refusal (`statusCode: 409`, `code`) that the door's own `catch` renders through `errorFromThrown` (`thrownAnswerOf` reads `.statusCode` and `.code`); the flow door renders the same thrown shape inside `land` and `registerAndSaveFlow` withdraws the engine registration on a refused landing (`restoreFlowRegistration`). The message names the condition, the consequence, the recipe D1 prescribes word for word (「run the change on a single replica or through the CLI, then restart every replica」) and ends "Nothing was changed or written", true at every refusal site.
7. **Caller class — RIGHT.** An `isSystem` caller is refused too (D1 names doors, not callers; the change still reaches one replica); a caller without `manage_metadata` still gets the `403` first, and the walled `403` precedes the `409` as well.
8. **Driver read — RIGHT.** `packageChangeReachesOneReplica` reads the `cluster` slot per request through `deps.resolveService`, whose chain tries the request kernel, the scoped default kernel and the default kernel's services map, so a project kernel reaches a root-composed cluster service; a throw or an absent slot answers `undefined` (single node), the same contract `composedClusterDriver` states. The module re-reads the driver over the async deps rather than importing `composedClusterDriver` because the dispatcher's probe is async and chain-aware; the predicate itself is still the shared one, so the two refusals cannot drift on the condition.
9. **Single node — RIGHT.** Every added path is `if (!(await packageChangeReachesOneReplica(...))) return null`; on a single node each door gains one service probe and nothing else. The 28 CONTROL cases and the state-file CONTROL pin that enable/disable still write `OS_HOME/package-state` on a single node. R3 holds; the split-brain guard is untouched.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/31599-runtime-package-doors-multi-replica-refusal.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/spec`, the two packages the diff moves; `@objectstack/service-cluster` is unmoved and correctly absent. `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and the changeset is right: no key a metadata author writes changes. Under maintainer ruling A on #25105 (the Check Changeset step of `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`: the level follows the Metadata-protocol line alone; `none` ⇒ `patch`; a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its carriers) the level is `patch`. The BREAKING banner and the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker are present and right: nothing authorable is removed or renamed, nothing to migrate, no tombstone. `Check Changeset`: success.
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — …` — RIGHT.** The value names both halves: narrowed (the seven doors and the two clone doors under the condition), widened (the runtime ledger row). The arm is the first token inside the parenthesis (`clause2-line.mjs` reads it so). It is the correction the prior record asked of #31712, carried here from the start by amendment 6728532665. Tier: the ledger path alone already puts the review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; the arm agrees.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note owed. `Implemented-by` is the dev's branch per the claim (`mode:thread`, dev session `session_01ADHkmPnqZD15YnBkNbm1jJ`).
- Dev deviation 1 (spec `check:test-typecheck` out of heap at 4096 MB, green at 8192): **noted, not relied on.** The head's check-runs are the gate verdicts. At the time of this record `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, every Lint job, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build UI Deps`, `PR-body guards` are `success`; `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Build Core`, `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Test UI (1–16/16)`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI` are `in_progress`; nothing is `failure`. The landing precondition is the seat's to read at enqueue time.
- Dev deviation 2 (branch restarted fresh at `cecb6bff` after GitHub deleted the merged branch; no history overwritten): **accepted**, a process note with no effect on the tree.
- Dev deviation 3 (runtime suite and gates ran on `cecb6bff`; `5eb211c4` adds one collection-time import for `check:test-source-alias`): **noted, not relied on**; the head's own check-runs govern, and the alias gate is inside the green lint jobs.
- Seat ruling A, Q1 (one code): **agreed.** D1 asks for 「one stable error code」 and item 2 asks for the shared predicate; the code is the shared constant, imported.
- Seat ruling A, Q2 (R6-style recipe wording): **agreed.** The sentence is D1's own recipe verbatim; `multiReplicaPackageChangeMessage` is its one spelling.
- Seat ruling A, Q3 (runtime's own ledger row, no second waiver): **agreed** (①.4, ①.5).
- `open_questions`: none declared.
- Out-of-scope note (protocol-internal `ensureCustomizationPackage` callers in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, i.e. `os migrate packageless-overlays`): **agreed, outside the card.** It is a CLI path, which is the recipe's own path. No carrier filed by this record.

### ④ Design judgment

1. **`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` (hits) — holds for the seven doors; one sentence does not hold in the tree (④.2).** The row sits under `@objectstack/runtime` (lines 304–582 of the head), the emitting package; its comment states the status (409), the moment (after authorization, before anything is written), the condition (`declaresMultiReplicaOnRedis`, named by package), the seven doors by path, and points at the cloud-connection row and PROVENANCE_WAIVERS for the shared string. Sentence by sentence against the tree: the seven doors agree (①.1); "plus the flow and permission-set clone doors when the copy would CREATE the source's paired customization package" does not agree for a base that is a member of an installed App (④.2). The comment's "right after the caller's authorization" is loose (the walled refusal also answers first; the changeset says so exactly): nit, ④.6. Not a finding: the row's order inside the runtime tuple (no gate orders rows; `check-error-code-casing` reads casing, duplication and shadowing only).
2. **`packages/runtime/src/multi-replica-package-refusal.ts` — `packageChangeReachesOneReplica` and `refuseMultiReplicaPackageChange` hold; `multiReplicaPairCreationRefusal` — MUST-FIX.** The probe derives the pair as `customizationPackageId(basePackageId)`, i.e. `BASE.custom`, and reads `registry.getPackage` of that id. The ensure it guards derives the pair as `pairOf(baseId, installedManifestsOfEngine(engine))` (`protocol-customization-package.ts` line 305), which is `customizationPackageId(appOf(base))`: for a base that declares one installed App, directly or through its declared parents, the pair is `APP.custom`, not `BASE.custom` (`@objectstack/metadata-core` `customization-pair-lookup.ts`, ruling record 6691022506; the ensure module's header: everything the pair is made of is "its App's … ⛔ never a local spelling"). The two derivations agree only for an App or an own-unit base. Consequences, each under declared replicas on Redis only (single node is unchanged, so R3 holds):
   - Under-refusal, the D1 defect: a legacy per-package pair `BASE.custom` installed (ADR-0146 D3 merge question 12 keeps it served until the migration ceremony) while `APP.custom` is absent: the probe answers "pair exists", returns `null`, and the ensure CREATES `APP.custom` through `installPackage` on this replica alone. The card's "Done when" ("no runtime package operation can leave replicas divergent") is not met on that state.
   - Over-refusal with a recipe that cannot unblock: an App-member source whose App pair `APP.custom` this replica already serves (the ensure would reuse it, creating nothing) is refused anyway, because `BASE.custom` is not in the registry, and the message tells the operator that `'BASE.custom' does not exist yet`: a package the ensure door never creates. Following the recipe (ensure on a single replica, restart every replica) creates `APP.custom`, which the probe never reads, so the clone stays refused.
   Neither suite can see it: the flow rig's `BASE` is `type: 'app'` and the permission-set double derives the pair as base + `.custom` itself. Fix: derive the pair with `pairOf(base, installedManifestsOf(registry))` from `@objectstack/metadata-core` (already a dependency of `@objectstack/runtime`, `package.json` line 62), answering `null` for any `!ok` derivation exactly as now (the ensure's own refusals follow), and pin an App-member base in both suites: App pair present ⇒ 200 and no package created; App pair absent ⇒ 409 naming `APP.custom`. Nothing about the seven package doors moves.
3. **`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` — holds.** Seven sites, one shape each, the subject in the walled refusal's gerund, placed identically after the walled refusal and before the closed-query check (①.1). The seven unrefused walled sites are the metadata writes (①.2). The route ledger declares no per-route codes for the walled refusal either, so no second declaration is owed.
4. **`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` — holds structurally; inherits ④.2; one nit.** The probe is asked inside `land`, so every judgement that needs no pair (501, the omitted-`package` 400, the explicit target's rule) still answers before anything is registered, and a refused landing withdraws the registration through the door's existing undo (①.6). Nit (④.7): the probe runs before the ensure's own refusals, so under the condition a writable, kernel or namespace-less base answers the multi-replica code with a "creating it" message where the ensure would have refused for its own reason; 409 either way, nothing written. The permission-set door is precise here (writable and kernel bases are judged before `beforeEnsure`); aligning the flow door is optional and can ride ④.2's fix.
5. **`packages/runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.ts` — holds; inherits ④.2.** `beforeEnsure` is asked after the writable and kernel judgements and after the 501, immediately before `ensureCustomizationPackage`, so nothing has been written when it throws; the door's one `catch` renders the thrown 409 with the code (①.6). `resolveDefaultCloneLanding` has no other caller in the tree, so the new optional parameter widens nothing a second caller relies on.
6. **Nit (hits file, prose) — the row comment's "right after the caller's authorization".** The walled-catalog refusal also answers first at every door; say "after the `manage_metadata` gate and the walled-catalog refusal" as the changeset does. No effect on correctness; the head moves for ④.2 anyway, so the dev may tighten it in the same push.
7. **Nit — the flow door's probe precedes the ensure's own refusals** (④.4). Harmless under the condition, invisible on a single node.

Tests, read as evidence only (lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`): 64 new cases in the three existing harnesses pin both declarations × the seven doors with every registry and protocol writer unrun and `OS_HOME` empty, the `isSystem` refusal, the gate order, 28 CONTROL topologies, the single-node state-file control, the five unrefused metadata doors, the clone doors' refusal/reuse/explicit-target/CONTROL matrix. They match the contract the implementing files state for an App or own-unit base; ④.2 names the one base shape they do not reach.

Findings: 1 must-fix (④.2, `multi-replica-package-refusal.ts`, inherited by the two clone doors) · 0 should-fix · 2 nits (④.6, ④.7). The must-fix earns a delta review of its fix by this reviewer on the new head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fad89bdc924ba15afbfaafb36e1be9b8f4d135a2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/multi-replica-package-refusal.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.ts (the narrowing face: every non-prose path of the diff; the three test files were read as evidence, the changeset is a prose face for the lane seat's ACCEPT)

Delta review of the round-1 fixes to record 6730977111 (head `5eb211c4`, FAIL on one must-fix). Inputs: the net diff `5eb211c4..fad89bdc` on `claude/project-thread-cn42eu` (two commits, `60c12f60` the fix and `fad89bdc` a one-line test typing; four files: `multi-replica-package-refusal.ts`, the ledger, `automation-flow-clone-custom-package.test.ts`, `permission-set-clone.test.ts`); the card and PR comments since the record (card: none since the os-dev-report 6730804450; PR: the seat's claim line 6731913187 for this head; the dev's round-1 report reached this record through the seat and is read as the dev's claim, never as the verdict); the check-runs on `fad89bdc`. The whole-PR judgments of the prior record stand where the tree did not move: `packages.ts`, `automation.ts` and `permission-set-clone.ts` are byte-identical to `5eb211c4`, the changeset and the PR body's declaration lines are unchanged. Code outside the diff (`@objectstack/metadata-core` `customization-pair-lookup.ts`, the protocol's ensure door and its save gate, `new-similar-target.ts`) was read to judge the diff, never reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The must-fix (④.2 of the prior record) — FIXED, RIGHT.** `multiReplicaPairCreationRefusal` now derives the pair as `pairOf(basePackageId, installedManifestsOf(registry))` from `@objectstack/metadata-core` (root-exported through `export * from './customization-pair-lookup.js'`; runtime already depends on the package), the same derivation the ensure door uses (`pairOf(baseId, installedManifestsOfEngine(engine))`, where `installedManifestsOfEngine(engine)` is `installedManifestsOf(engine.registry)`). Read against the lookup: an App or own-unit base derives BASE.custom as before; a member of one installed App derives APP.custom; several Apps with no namespace pick derive `no_single_app`, which is `!ok` and answers `null`, leaving the ensure's own 409. `installedManifestsOf` of an absent registry is the empty lookup (every package its own unit), so a rig with no `registry` degrades to the prior behaviour rather than throwing. The three consequences the prior record named are closed in the tree: a member whose App pair this replica serves answers `null` (the ensure reuses, creates nothing); a member whose App pair is absent is refused naming APP.custom, the package the ensure would create; a legacy per-member pair present with the App pair absent is refused too, because the ensure would still create APP.custom on this replica. R3 unchanged: the probe still begins with `packageChangeReachesOneReplica`, so a single node never reaches the derivation.
2. **The hits-file sentence — now agrees with the tree.** The ledger comment reads "when the copy would CREATE the source's paired customization package (its App's pair, `pairOf`)"; the probe reads exactly that pair. ④.6 is also fixed: "right after the caller's authorization and the walled-catalog refusal (both still answer first)". No other ledger byte moves: the row, its owner key, the union and the waiver table are as on `5eb211c4` (①.4 and ①.5 of the prior record stand; `Lint · docs & code guards` success on this head).
3. **Narrowing declared vs tree — RIGHT.** The PR body's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — …` sentence for the clone doors ("only when their default landing would create the source's paired customization package on this replica") is now true for every base shape, not only for an App or own-unit base. Nothing else declared moves.
